author: val
body: This is the widget walk every GuiOS APPLICATION paints through. UI GpuRender.gr-render-tree is apps/cvmm only, via AppRunner.bare-app-render; GuiShell.composite-walk-gpu is the shell chrome only. The three walks are not in competition: each covers exactly the widget kinds its own consumer builds, and GuiShell's narrow one is deliberate because citing the library dispatch there would draw every label twice, in two fonts, at two positions.

author: val
body: The value is held inside its own bounds before the width is taken. An unheld value above the maximum draws a fill wider than the widget and paints over whatever sits beside it; a negative one asks for a negative width. Measured before the fix against seed 6867EA9D: a gauge at 150 of 100 in a 200-pixel box read inside 1 / outside 1. Pinned by codex/test/gop-render-clamp.

author: val
body: There are THREE gauge renderers in the tree, not two. UI GpuRender and codex/test/gpu-gauge-clamp both say the framebuffer compositor has always clamped, and that is true of Works GopComposite.comp-gauge-fill. It was never true of this one, and a check that compared two functions was read as an answer about three. Enumerate the implementations before acting on any claim that the other implementation does X.

author: val
body: The caret is held inside its own content box, both ends. Six pixels per character of cursor index leaves the widget as soon as the index passes the box width, and a filter or search box that sets its cursor to the length of its text grows the index with each keystroke. The low end is held because a negative index would paint left of the box. Measured before the fix: box 1, inside 0, outside 1, the caret entirely outside the widget.

author: val
body: gop-render-label, gop-render-button and gop-render-input draw through gop-buf-put-text-role-clip rather than gop-buf-put-text-role because they are the callers that know a box: content is already computed here for the origin, and its right edge is the bound. An application drawing free-standing text still reaches the unbounded name and is unaffected, which is why the bounded form is a separate name rather than an added parameter.

author: val
body: Clipping is the whole of what landed. Ellipsis is a presentation choice that sits above a clipping primitive and needs no new state; scrolling to keep a caret visible applies only to inputs and needs a per-widget view offset, which WidgetNode has nowhere to hold. Both are open and neither is bundled.
